mathematical_premises.statement: The target small-ball functional is coordinatewise linear in each input density for a fixed output event.
mathematical_premises.scope: Fixed measurable output event and fixed other coordinate laws.

mathematical_premises.statement: Lebesgue measure is non-atomic, so the bathtub optimizer under 0<=f<=1 and integral 1 is an indicator of a set of measure 1.
Compact completion by a disjoint indicator filler preserves density height <=1 and total mass 1.

proved_results: Exact no-loss reduction from arbitrary input supports to compactly supported admissible product densities for any measurable pushforward map.
Uniform compact-support output Fourier-L1 bounds pass to arbitrary supports with the same constant by L1 completion, characteristic-function convergence and Fatou.
For fixed small-ball events, compact admissible product densities reduce exactly to indicator densities of coordinate sets of measure 1.
Full QFORM bounded-density target with constant C is equivalent to the same geometric small-ball inequality for coordinate sets that are finite unions of bounded intervals of total length 1.
Translation covariance introduces only the linear term 2(Aa)^T y and leaves the Hessian spectrum unchanged.

partner_result_applied.application: Its weighted-Wiener/Fourier route may be reduced to compactly supported input laws without any tail or moment argument; the same Fourier-L1 constant transfers by Fatou.

assigned_partner_status: No completed current-qform account03/B14 handoff was visible at source read.
unresolved_implication: Prove a dimension-free bound |{x in product E_i: x^T A x in I}| <= C|I| uniformly for finite-union coordinate sets E_i of measure 1, with no dependence on fragment count, diameter, location or separation, for every rotated indefinite A with at least three eigenvalues of magnitude >=1; or construct a genuine counterexample in this reduced class.
next_step: Attack the reduced finite-union geometry directly by an aggregation inequality that does not sum a constant over components; alternatively apply compactification to the selected-large-mode weighted Wiener estimate from account03/B05.
correction_status: Pointwise law-uniform Fresnel decay remains refuted even in the reduced finite-union class; no corrected claim uses it.
